title: Archiving Portuguese Legislative Debates
business: Municipal legislative bodies managing thousands of hours of recorded audio from public sessions.
problem: Legislative records are currently stored as raw audio files, making it impossible for citizens or staff to search for specific policy discussions, motions, or speaker mentions without manual listening.
solution: The wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-portuguese model provides an automated speech-to-text pipeline that converts these audio archives into searchable text transcripts, enabling keyword indexing and content discovery.
steps: Standardize all incoming legislative audio recordings to a 16kHz sampling rate to match model requirements.
Initialize the Wav2Vec2ForCTC model and processor using the jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-portuguese weights.
Implement a batch processing script to iterate through audio files, converting them into numerical arrays.
Pass the processed arrays through the model to generate text transcriptions for each session.
Store the resulting text in a database linked to the original audio timestamps for retrieval.
outcome: A fully searchable digital archive where staff can instantly locate specific legislative debates by querying keywords, significantly reducing administrative research time.
limitation: The model requires audio input sampled at exactly 16kHz; failure to resample audio correctly will result in degraded transcription accuracy or processing errors during inference.

code.content:
import librosa
from transformers import Wav2Vec2ForCTC, Wav2Vec2Processor

# Load model and processor
processor = Wav2Vec2Processor.from_pretrained("jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-portuguese")
model = Wav2Vec2ForCTC.from_pretrained("jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-portuguese")

# Ensure audio is 16kHz as required
audio, sr = librosa.load("session_recording.wav", sr=16000)

# Process and transcribe
inputs = processor(audio, sampling_rate=16000, return_tensors="pt")
logits = model(**inputs).logits
predicted_ids = torch.argmax(logits, dim=-1)
transcription = processor.batch_decode(predicted_ids)
